text:
elaine.docs: Opening a small PR to change the SOC2-friendly wording around audit log retention + add SDK snippets for TTL + legal-hold behavior. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/982

tony-pe: Thanks — can you call out the operator-visible behavior vs customer API fields? We need to avoid implying logs are deleted immediately during legal hold.

elaine.docs: Yep — plan is to describe three surface behaviors: 1) customer TTL (api.retention_seconds) 2) legal hold flag (tenant.legal_hold=true) which supersedes TTL for export/API read access, and 3) internal archival (S3 lifecycle).

julian: Also add a short code snippet for node/go showing the header we set for TTL and the redaction toggle. That helps SDK owners sync the examples.

elaine.docs: Draft snippets added in PR — copying here for quick review:

```bash
# curl: create export with 30d retention (in seconds) and redaction enabled
curl -X POST  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"  -H "Content-Type: application/json"  -d '{"scope":"audit_export","retention_seconds":2592000,"redact_pii":true}'  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/exports
```

```javascript
// node: pass retention and redact flags in request body
const res = await client.createExport({
  scope: 'audit_export',
  retention_seconds: 2592000, // 30 days
  redact_pii: true
});
```

```go
// go: example for retention + legal hold check (pseudo)
req := &CreateExportRequest{
  Scope: "audit_export",
  RetentionSeconds: 2592000,
  RedactPII: true,
}
resp, err := client.CreateExport(ctx, req)
```

samir-eng: Couple of nitpicks: 1) spell out that retention_seconds is a best-effort deletion window for exported/downloadable artifacts; internal immutable journal for SOC2 evidence is retained per contract but access can be restricted. 2) clarify that legal_hold prevents automated deletion but does not bypass approved manual deletion workflows (ops + legal).

elaine.docs: Good call. I'll add a small 'operational note' section. Proposed phrasing: "Legal hold will mark tenant data as non-expirable for automated retention enforcement; manual deletion requires explicit authorization and audit." Thoughts?

julian: That's concise. Maybe add an example sentence: "If a tenant sets retention_seconds to 0 while legal_hold=true, logs remain available to support and compliance until legal_hold is removed or a manual disposition is approved."

tony-pe: +1. Also add an explicit example for the SDK migration guide — how to detect legal_hold responses from the export status API so client code can surface a helpful message to users. Something like:

```json
{
  "export_id":"exp_abc123",
  "status":"held",
  "legal_hold":true,
  "retention_seconds":0
}
```

elaine.docs: Adding that JSON sample. I'll also update the docs checklist: 
- update SOC2 wording to avoid "delete on request" implication
- include curl/node/go snippets (done)
- add migration note for SDKs to handle 'held' state
- link to internal legal guidance (redacted link in PR)

compliance-bot: Reminder: When changing retention language, run the SOC2 wording linter and tag @legal-review for signoff.

elaine.docs: on it — pinging @legal-review in the PR description. Also adding changelog footnote: "clarifies retention vs. legal hold; adds SDK examples and export-state guidance."

samir-eng: Very small runtime note: our export service currently enforces deletion via a scheduled job; legal_hold flips a flag that excludes tenant records from that job. Add that technical detail to avoid confusion for engineers reading the doc.

elaine.docs: added a short 'how it works (ops)' paragraph: "Export deletion job skips records where tenant.legal_hold = true; when legal_hold is cleared, the normal retention window resumes from that point."

tony-pe: LGTM. Once legal signs off, we can merge. Thanks for the fast turnaround, @elaine.docs :thumbsup:

elaine.docs: thanks all — merging after legal review. If anything else pops up I'll follow up in this thread. :spiral_note_pad:
